questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions that the Vice-President of India shall be the ex officio Chairman of the Council of States?
questions.solution: Article 89 specifies that the Vice-President of India shall be the ex officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha). This is a unique position where the Vice-President, who is not a member of the House, presides over its proceedings. Note: Article 64 also mentions this dual role.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India?

A. Original jurisdiction extends to any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between the Government of India and any State or States on one side and one or more States on the other or between two or more States.

B. Appellate Jurisdiction extends when the Union plus some States are one side and some other States on the other side of the dispute.

C. Under Articles 129 and 142 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court has been vested with the power to punish for contempt of court.

D.As of now, the International Commercial Arbitration cannot be initiated in the Supreme Court.
questions.solution: Statements A and C are correct. (A) The Original Jurisdiction (Article 131) covers disputes between the Union and States or between States. (C) Articles 129 and 142 empower the Supreme Court to punish for contempt of court to maintain its dignity. Correction: Appellate jurisdiction relates to hearing appeals from lower courts, and International Commercial Arbitration *can* be initiated in the SC under certain conditions.

questions.question: Directive Principles of State Policy in India have been taken from the Constitution of which country?
questions.solution: The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) were borrowed from the Irish Constitution (Constitution of Ireland). The Irish, in turn, had taken this concept from the Spanish Constitution. These principles are listed in Part IV of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Abolition of titles is mentioned in which Article of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: Article 18 deals with the Abolition of Titles. It prohibits the State from conferring any title (except military or academic distinctions) and forbids Indian citizens from accepting any title from a foreign state. This is part of the Right to Equality.

questions.question: In case the President is satisfied with the Governor’s report, he may declare President’s Rule under Article 356 but such proclamation is initially for a period of ________.
questions.solution: When President’s Rule is declared under Article 356, the proclamation is initially valid for a period of six months. It must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months of its issuance. It can be extended for a maximum of three years with periodic approvals every six months.

questions.question: When was the ‘The Objective Resolution’ moved by Pt. Jawahar Lal Nehru?
questions.solution: Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic 'Objective Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946. This resolution outlined the fundamental goals and philosophy of the Constitution and eventually became the basis for the Preamble.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The State shall endeavour to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines’?
questions.solution: Article 48 directs the State to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines. It also specifically mentions taking steps for preserving and improving breeds and prohibiting the slaughter of cows, calves, and other milch and draught cattle.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions about the right of the Advocate-General of a state to speak in the State Legislature?
questions.solution: Article 177 gives the Advocate-General of a state (as well as State Ministers) the right to speak and participate in the proceedings of the State Legislature or its committees, even if they are not members. However, they do not have the right to vote.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the state’?
questions.solution: Article 164(2) mandates that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State. This means the entire ministry falls if it loses the confidence of the lower house, ensuring executive accountability to the elected representatives.

questions.question: Article 21 is related to which of the following fundamental rights?
questions.option_3: Protection of Language, Culture of Minorities
questions.option_4: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty
questions.solution: Article 21 guarantees the Protection of Life and Personal Liberty. It states that no person shall be deprived of their life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. The Supreme Court has expanded this to include rights like privacy, shelter, and health.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions about the salaries and allowances of members of the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council of a state?
questions.solution: Article 195 deals with the salaries and allowances of members of the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council. It states that members are entitled to receive such salaries as may from time to time be determined by the Legislature of the State by law.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that a person may be appointed as the Governor of two or more states?
questions.solution: Article 153 originally stated there shall be a Governor for each state, but the 7th Amendment (1956) added a proviso that the same person can be appointed as Governor for two or more states. This is often done for administrative convenience in smaller states or UTs.

questions.question: Which Article specifies the procedure for amending the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: Article 368 in Part XX of the Constitution specifies the procedure for amending the Constitution. It empowers Parliament to add, vary, or repeal any provision through a special majority, though it cannot alter the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.

questions.question:
Who among the following are eligible for free legal aid under the National Legal Services Authority?

A.A member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.

B.A victim of trafficking in human beings or beggar as referred to in Article 23 of the Constitution

C.An industrial workman

D.A person under circumstances of undeserved want such as being a victim of a mass disasters

E.To file any case in Supreme Court, if any person need free legal aid, the person’s annual income must be below 10 lakhs.
questions.option_2: A, B, C and D only
questions.option_3: A, B, C, D and E
questions.solution: Statements A, B, C, and D are correct. Eligible groups for free legal aid include SC/ST members, victims of trafficking/begar, industrial workmen, and victims of mass disasters. Correction: Statement E is wrong; the income limit for the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee is generally 5 lakhs (or as notified), not 10 lakhs.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution states that “There shall be a High Court for each state”?
questions.solution: Article 214 of the Indian Constitution states that 'There shall be a High Court for each State.' However, Parliament has the power to establish a common High Court for two or more states or for two or more states and a Union Territory.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘All the executive action of the Government of a state shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor’?
questions.solution: Article 166(1) provides that all executive actions of the Government of a State shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor. Even though the real power lies with the Chief Minister, the Governor remains the formal head of the state executive.

questions.question: Article 50 of the Constitution of India refers to the ________.
questions.solution: Article 50 directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State. This ensures the independence of the judiciary and prevents executive interference in judicial functions.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions about the qualification for membership of the State Legislature?
questions.solution: Article 173 lays down the qualifications for membership of the State Legislature. Key requirements include being a citizen of India and being at least 25 years old for the Legislative Assembly or 30 years old for the Legislative Council.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Union Executive?
questions.solution: The Union Executive is dealt with in Articles 52 to 78 under Part V of the Constitution. It consists of the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, and the Attorney General of India.

questions.question: Directive Principles of State Policy comes under which Article?
questions.solution: The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are contained in Articles 36 to 51 under Part IV of the Constitution. They are guidelines for the government to establish social and economic democracy in the country.

questions.question: What Article of the Indian Constitution provides that the State Governor has the authority to reserve a bill for the consideration of the President?
questions.solution: Article 200 gives the State Governor the authority to reserve a bill passed by the state legislature for the consideration of the President. This is a crucial link in India's federal structure where the Union keeps a check on state legislation.

questions.question: The concept of limited government is a major advancement to protect the _______ of the citizens from the ruling governments.
questions.solution: The concept of limited government is designed to protect the Fundamental Rights of citizens. By placing constitutional limits on the powers of the ruling government, it prevents arbitrary rule and ensures that individual liberties are not encroached upon.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the annual financial statement of the Government of India?
questions.solution: Article 112 deals with the Annual Financial Statement, popularly known as the Budget. It is a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for a particular financial year.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that, where the same person is appointed as the Governor of two or more states, the emoluments and allowances payable to him/her shall be allocated among those states?
questions.solution: Article 158 outlines the conditions of the Governor's office. It specifies that when one person is Governor of multiple states, their emoluments and allowances are shared among the states in such proportion as the President may determine by order.

questions.question: In which Article does the Finance Commission of India find a mention?
questions.solution: The Finance Commission of India is a quasi-judicial body established under Article 280. It is constituted by the President every five years to recommend the distribution of financial resources between the Union and the States.

questions.question: Biological Diversity Act 2002 was passed by the Government of India. It fulfilled ideals of which article of Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution: The Biological Diversity Act 2002 fulfills the ideals of Article 48A. This DPSP (added by the 42nd Amendment) mandates that the State shall endeavor to protect and improve the environment and safeguard the forests and wildlife of the country.

questions.question: As per Article ________ of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
questions.solution: As per Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. This means the government remains in office only as long as it maintains the majority support in the lower house of Parliament.
